transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alicia, Marcus, Priya (Redwood); Kevin, Sara, Tomás, Emily (BlueHarbor)
Shared: Deck (link), runbook template, pricing worksheet (Alicia to share)

Summary:
Quick check-in for week 3 of the pilot capacity sprint. Primary goals: review last week's burst rehearsal results, finalize autoscale and reserve buffer strategy for Dedicated, agree on throughput headroom for the pilot, and align on next bench runs. Customer wants a clear failover/backoff policy and visibility into tail latency during promo events.

Topics:
- burst simulation outcomes
- autoscale windows and cooldowns
- reserve buffer vs burst credits tradeoffs
- KV cache warmup and prefix caching impact
- Private/VPC considerations and SOC2/KMS checklist

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia: hey everybody, thanks for joining. we'll try to keep this tight, we've got 57 minutes on the calendar, um, quick roll-call?
[00:08] Kevin: yeah Kevin here, um, VP eng at BlueHarbor.
[00:12] Sara: sara platform.
[00:14] Tomás: tomás devops.
[00:16] Emily: emily product.
[00:18] Marcus: marcus from Redwood, solutions eng.
[00:20] Priya: priya CSM.
[00:22] Alicia: great. quick agenda, recap the burst rehearsal from Friday, talk autoscale tuning (cooldowns, thresholds), discuss reserve buffer sizing, and agree next steps for bench. Marcus you pulled the logs?
[00:31] Marcus: yep pulled them, ran a couple of variations. friday run was a 5-minute 2x sustained traffic spike against the Dedicated pilot nodes with prefix caching enabled. results are in the deck — main thing: p95 stayed stable ~120 ms, p99 spiked to around 750ms for a short window when the KV cache warmed, and we saw about a 6% token loss rate on one microsecond — sorry one min — one minute of the spike where requests queued beyond our 500ms soft SLO.
[01:05] Tomás: queued beyond 500? ok that aligns with what we saw in the customer logs where nginx backed up, we had a couple of timeouts.
[01:12] Sara: can you explain the KV cache bit — are we seeing cold-start on kv?
[01:16] Marcus: yeah so the prefix/KV cache has a warmup time. during the first 30 seconds of the spike, a lot of requests missed the cache and those requests pay the full attention compute cost. after ~45 seconds the cache hit rate climbed to 92% and latency normalized. in practice for BlueHarbor a 30-45s warmup during a promo is realistic unless you pre-warm.
[01:42] Emily: pre-warm how? like send synthetic traffic?
[01:44] Marcus: exactly, either synthetic walker traffic or a lightweight prefetcher. Redwood can run a pre-warm phase as part of the runbook, that's part of the rehearsal we recommend.
[01:54] Alicia: quick note — we'll include the pre-warm step in the runbook we hand off, and also options for prefix caching TTL adjustments.
[01:59] Kevin: okay, so if we need that warmup, what's the tradeoff on cost vs latency?
[02:04] Marcus: pre-warm adds token/warmup compute cost but saves tail latency and avoids user-facing errors. the reserve buffer is cheaper than keeping all nodes at peak — but depends on how long spikes last.
[02:15] Priya: just to add, customers often pick a small reserve buffer to cover micro spikes, and then burst credits for sustained promos.
[02:23] Kevin: what's a 'small' reserve buffer for our numbers?
[02:26] Marcus: for your baseline and peak samples — from last week's traffic — we recommend a 20% reserve buffer for normal peaks and plan a 2x burst credit runway for sustained promotional bursts >2 minutes. that gave us acceptable p99 in the sim.
[02:41] Tomás: 2x burst credits means what in practice? do we get billed per token? how immediate is it?
[02:48] Alicia: it's immediate; burst credits are drawn from your account and we bill per-usage. reserve buffer is capacity reserved in Dedicated so you pay the monthly reserved rate, which is higher baseline but predictable.
[02:59] Kevin: predictable pricing is nice for finance but we want an ops-first route — if a promo goes sideways, we need graceful degradation not hard failures. what are fallback policies?
[03:11] Marcus: we suggest multilayer fallback: first, degrade non-essential prompts (lower temperature, reduce max tokens), second, fallback to smaller model variant with faster kernels, third, rate-limit per-token for anonymous vs authenticated users. Redwood routing can do regional fallback or model variant fallback automatically.
[03:30] Emily: can that routing be policy-based per-route? like product reviews vs checkout?
[03:33] Marcus: yes, per-route policy is supported in the config. you can pin checkout to strict latency SLO and reviews to cost-saving fallback.
[03:41] Sara: we noticed a weird OCR of 'KV cash' in the log sometimes, is that a transcription issue?
[03:45] Marcus: that's the transcriber, yes it's KV cache.
[03:47] Kevin: also about autoscale cooldowns — last run it seemed the autoscaler tripped too late, causing a backlog. can we shorten cooldowns?
[03:54] Marcus: cooldowns are a tunable parameter. right now pilot is at 90s cooldown and scale step of 1 node. two levers: reduce cooldown to 45s and increase step to 2 nodes during promo windows to avoid cascading queueing. downside is you risk overprovisioning for short bursts.
[04:12] Tomás: what's the minimum safe cooldown for memory-heavy models? we saw OOMs before when the cluster resized too fast.
[04:19] Marcus: cool down too low can cause thrash. we suggest 45–60s for your current model family; if you bump step size, increase headroom per node (e.g., reserve buffer) to avoid OOM.
[04:30] Kevin: ok, show me the numbers from Friday's rehearsal again — p99 at 750ms only during cache warmup, correct?
[04:37] Marcus: correct. most of the spike window p95 was 120ms, p99 peaked twice at ~750ms for 10–20s each. overall token throughput hit 2.1x baseline. error rate was low except for the 60s window where queueing hit timeouts.
[04:55] Emily: did you run with quantized model variant? will that help tail latency?
[04:58] Marcus: we tested q8 and q4 variants; q8 reduced median token cost and sometimes improved latency, but for p99 we still saw similar tail behavior because it's not the compute precision, it's cache warmup and queueing. quantization helps cost but doesn't remove the warmup problem.
[05:18] Priya: reminder — Redwood can recommend a quantization profile by workload; we'll attach suggested configs.
[05:23] Kevin: what about prefix caching TTLs? can we lengthen TTLs so repeated calls hit cache across sessions?
[05:28] Marcus: yes, TTLs are adjustable but need memory tradeoffs. longer TTL = more KV memory. we can simulate different TTLs in the next bench run to measure hit-rate delta.
[05:38] Tomás: on Private — we might need to run on-prem for compliance on a small set of endpoints. what's the difference in behavior for warmup and burst on Private vs Hosted?
[05:47] Marcus: behavior is consistent functionally but you control networking and caching tiers. Private may have slightly higher cold-starts initially if your on-prem nodes are heavier or have slower interconnects; we'd advise a pre-warm strategy and local cache warming scripts. also KMS/HSM integration is available if you need key separation.
[06:03] Sara: can you confirm SOC2 artifacts? our security team will ask.
[06:07] Alicia: yes, we'll upload SOC2 report, KMS integration guide, audit-log format, and RBAC examples to the shared folder after the call.
[06:14] Kevin: timeline question — we want a production guardrail before the big sale in three weeks, what's realistic?
[06:18] Priya: with the current momentum, probably 2 weeks to lock autoscale policies and reserve buffer, 1 more week for runbook rehearsal and handoff, so 3 weeks is tight but doable if bench runs go well.
[06:29] Marcus: to be safe we should run a 10-minute sustained 2x burst in the next 5 business days to validate the reserve buffer sizing. that will expose warmup and any OOMs.
[06:39] Kevin: ok do it. I'll upload the traffic sample by Monday.
[06:42] Alicia: noted. Marcus you'll own the bench?
[06:45] Marcus: yes.
[06:46] Emily: one edge case — we sometimes have sudden bursts from cron jobs (midnight ET) and they are very spiky, like 8–10 seconds. how should we tune for that?
[06:55] Marcus: for sub-10s spikes, reserve buffer helps but consider rate-limiting or queuing policies at the edge. also pre-schedule pre-warm if the cron is deterministic.
[07:04] Tomás: what about observability — we need token-level cost and per-route latency. can the console show that?
[07:09] Alicia: yes Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdown, p50/p95/p99, and you can hook traces to your tracer. we'll enable a dashboard for BlueHarbor.
[07:17] Sara: would you be able to add alerts for p99>500ms for more than 30s?
[07:21] Marcus: yes we can create an alert policy and tie it to slack and Opsgenie.
[07:25] Kevin: legal/procurement question: if we reserve buffer for the pilot and later scale to full production, is there a step-down penalty?
[07:33] Alicia: reserve contracts have minimum terms; for pilots we usually do a month-to-month pilot carve-out. Alicia: I'll include the contract excerpt in the pricing worksheet.
[07:42] Emily: any other surprises from the rehearsal logs?
[07:45] Marcus: just that a small percentage of requests hit a timeout at the ingress (nginx) before Redwood could respond; that's a config we can tune — increase keepalive and worker threads during promo windows.
[07:57] Tomás: good to know. I'll coordinate with infra.
[08:00] Priya: ok let's review accept criteria for the production guardrail: 1) <0.5% error rate across promo, 2) p99 < 800ms for the sustained bursts after pre-warm, 3) documented runbook and rollback plan, 4) alerting and cost thresholds configured.
[08:20] Kevin: that sounds reasonable. set the error bar to 0.5% and we'll accept the p99 goal.
[08:26] Alicia: recap quick: Marcus to run 10m 2x burst and share logs, Alicia to send pricing + contract excerpt + SOC2/KMS docs, Kevin to upload traffic sample, Tomás to confirm VPC peering/private trial availability, Priya to provision dashboard and alert.
[08:41] Emily: thanks everyone.
[08:43] Marcus: one more thing — we'll include the pre-warm script and a small synthetic generator in the repo so you can test locally. link in deck.
[08:52] Alicia: perfect. we'll follow up with a 30-minute bench readout next wednesday, same time. thanks all.
[08:58] Kevin: thanks. bye.
